title: Closure record / 闭合测量记录
description: One completed circuit of the leveling mechanism: depart from the origin, take an independent reading at each benchmark from a different review party, return, compute the closure error f, and compare it with the tolerance F. This proposal argues that a declaration nobody can machine-check is not evidence; the closure mechanism is its own central declaration, so it is specified here as a data contract rather than described only in prose. A record that validates against this schema can be recomputed by check_closure.js without reading the proposal.

disclaimer.description: Concept advice. A record is not an approval, an operating licence, or a government determination.

illustrative.description: True when the readings are worked examples rather than field measurements. The example shipped with this package sets it true; a real record must set it false and carry provenance for every reading.

route.description: Which closing route the circuit ran along.

tolerance_class.description: F1 bodily safety or administrative decisions; F2 individual rights; F3 information only.

tolerance_F.description: The tolerance in force for this cycle. May only tighten on evidence; it may never be loosened because a scenario failed to meet it.

f_convention.description: Which quantity each station's reading expresses. In every case f is the RANGE across stations — max(reading) minus min(reading) — which is what the proposal means by the maximum divergence between stations. All three conventions are deviations and never attainment scores, so f <= F is always the passing test; using an attainment score as f inverts it and would fail a scenario for agreeing 86% of the time. 1-minus-consistency: the station's consistency ratio on the published question set. satisfaction-range: the station's satisfaction score. false-positive-plus-false-negative: the sum of the two error rates measured at that station.

halved.description: True while the scenario is on a shortened cycle after resumption, until two further consecutive passes.

stations.description: Ordered stations of the circuit. At least three are needed for a closure error to mean anything, and the first must be the origin benchmark BM-0: every circuit departs from the origin. The circuit need not physically end at BM-0, because f is defined as the maximum divergence between stations rather than as a return difference — the four-week S08 trial runs a simplified three-station RT-N (BM-0, BM-303, BM-1) on exactly that basis.

benchmark.description: BM-0 origin, BM-1/BM-2 first order, BM-2x second order, BM-3xx third order.

review_party.description: Four categories, none omissible across a circuit. A reading is attributed to the party that took it, not to the party that owns the site.

reading.description: The station's measured value on the published question set, in the units the f_convention expects.

read_by_affected_user.description: True when the reading was taken in person by the population it concerns rather than on their behalf. Required true for wheelchair-passing and step-free items.

jurisdictions.description: Authorities whose boundary this point sits across. Every benchmark on this belt is a seam point, so a single-entry list should be justified.

f.description: The computed closure error. Recomputable from stations[] by check_closure.js; a record whose stated f disagrees with the recomputation is rejected.

action.description: continue when f <= F. return-whole-route when f > F: the whole route is re-measured and the scenario drops to its non-AI equivalent. Amending only the worst station is not an available action, which is why it is not in this enumeration.

non_ai_path_available.description: 必填，且只能为 true。此前该字段可选、检查器只拒绝显式 false，因此省略它即可通过——对本方案声称不可豁免的一条规则而言，这是 fail-open。由 PR #1002 的评审 @anselasimov-web 指出。

resumption.description: Present only when this record resumes a scenario that was previously returned. Exit is easy and return is slow, deliberately.

consecutive_passes.description: Two are required before resumption. Once may be luck.

unanimous_four_parties.description: Required true for an F1 safety incident. No majority rule.
